title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets for Firms
summary: A ten-module programme for firms designing, launching and running tokenised securities, funds and platforms, from business case and legal structure to custody, settlement and supervisory engagement.
intro: This training programme equips asset managers, investment firms, platforms and market infrastructures to design, launch and run tokenised securities and funds: building the business case, structuring the legal basis, choosing platforms, and managing custody, settlement and technology risk.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip firms to move from tokenisation pilots to products and services that are commercially sound, legally robust and operationally safe. Participants leave able to build and challenge a business case, structure and run a tokenised issuance, fund or platform, and evidence to supervisors that familiar standards on investor protection, custody and settlement are met.
sections.What It Covers: The business case for tokenisation, legal structuring and the link to the underlying asset, issuing and distributing tokenised securities, tokenised fund design and operations, collateral and treasury use cases, platform choice and ledger governance, settlement and the cash leg, custody and client asset protection, smart contract and interoperability risk, and the operating model and regulatory engagement.
Intended Audience: Product, strategy and digital assets leads at asset managers, investment firms, trading venues, CSDs and tokenisation platforms
Operations, transfer agency, custody, legal, compliance and risk staff responsible for tokenised products and services
Senior managers and project sponsors taking a tokenisation initiative from pilot to launch
Learning Objectives: Build and challenge a business case for tokenisation that separates genuine benefits from claims
Structure tokenised securities and funds so that legal ownership, investor rights and the ledger record align
Evaluate platform, ledger and cash leg options and their governance, settlement and interoperability consequences
Design custody, safekeeping and reconciliation arrangements that protect client assets on a ledger
Manage smart contract, technology and third-party risk across the tokenisation value chain
Design the operating model for a tokenised product and evidence its soundness to supervisors
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a five-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies and design exercises, ending with a launch workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's products and role in the value chain.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of securities, funds, custody or settlement operations is helpful. Some familiarity with crypto-assets or distributed ledgers is useful but not required.
Core Reading: FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Tokenisation (2024)
CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
BIS, Annual Economic Report 2023, Chapter III: Blueprint for the Future Monetary System

modules.title: Tokenisation Strategy and the Business Case
modules.summary: What tokenisation means in practice for a firm, where it creates real value in issuance, funds, collateral and settlement, and how to test a business case before committing capital and reputation.
objectives: Explain how a traditional asset is tokenised and the ledger designs that support it
Assess claimed benefits such as faster settlement, fractionalisation and programmability against current practice
Challenge a tokenisation business case on cost, demand, liquidity and dependency
syllabus: Tokens, ledgers, nodes and consensus for practitioners
Where value lies: issuance, funds, collateral, settlement and distribution
Strategic options: issue, distribute, custody, operate or partner
Business case tests: demand, secondary liquidity, cost and exit

modules.title: Legal Structuring of Tokenised Assets
modules.summary: How to structure a tokenised asset so that ownership, transfer and investor rights are legally certain, and how to resolve conflicts between the ledger and the legal record before launch.
objectives: Distinguish digitally native issuance, digital twins and depositary receipt structures
Determine when a token is a financial instrument and the consequences for the firm
Design legal documentation that aligns the ledger with the register of ownership
syllabus: Native tokens, digital twins and wrapped or receipt structures
Classification: financial instruments, fund units and other tokens
Ledger records, registers, governing law and conflict of laws
Insolvency remoteness, enforceability and investor rights

modules.title: Issuing and Distributing Tokenised Securities
modules.summary: How firms arrange, issue and distribute tokenised bonds and equities, the roles each party plays, and the disclosure, product governance and suitability duties that apply when products reach new investors.
objectives: Map the roles of issuer, arranger, registrar, platform operator and distributor
Prepare disclosure of the technology, legal and operational risks of a tokenised offering
Apply product governance and suitability to fractionalised and retail distribution
syllabus: The issuance lifecycle for a tokenised bond or equity
Roles, contracts and allocation of responsibilities
Disclosure of technology, ledger and counterparty risk
Fractionalisation, target market and retail suitability

modules.title: Tokenised Funds: Product Design and Operations
modules.summary: How fund managers and service providers design and operate tokenised share classes, including on-chain transfer agency, dealing and valuation, and the responsibilities of managers, depositaries and distributors.
objectives: Design a tokenised share class and its subscription, transfer and redemption flows
Adapt transfer agency, NAV calculation and investor registers to a ledger
Allocate oversight duties between the manager, depositary and distributors
syllabus: Tokenised share classes and on-chain transfer agency
Dealing cycles, NAV, redemption and liquidity management on a ledger
Investor onboarding, whitelisting and AML/CFT controls on transfer
Depositary oversight, distributor arrangements and secondary transfers

modules.title: Collateral, Repo and Treasury Use Cases
modules.summary: How firms use tokenised assets and tokenised money market fund shares for collateral, margin, intraday repo and cash management, and the legal, liquidity and operational risks of faster collateral movement.
objectives: Explain how tokenised assets are mobilised for collateral, margin and repo
Assess the enforceability of collateral arrangements and close-out on a ledger
Manage the liquidity and operational risks of faster collateral flows
syllabus: Collateral mobility, intraday repo and margin calls
Tokenised money market fund shares as collateral and cash management
Eligibility, haircuts, valuation and close-out netting
Interaction with central counterparties and margin frameworks

modules.title: Platform Choice and Ledger Governance
modules.summary: How to choose between building, joining or partnering on a tokenisation platform, the trade-offs between permissioned and public ledgers, and the governance rights the firm needs over the network it relies on.
objectives: Compare permissioned, public and hybrid ledgers for control, access and resilience
Assess platform operators, node arrangements and governance rights
Evaluate conflicts in platforms that combine issuance, trading, settlement and custody
syllabus: Build, join or partner: platform options and selection criteria
Permissioned, public and hybrid ledgers: governance and access
Node operation, upgrades, forks and change control
Vertical integration, conflicts of interest and licensing implications

modules.title: Settlement, the Cash Leg and Finality
modules.summary: How tokenised transactions settle, the options for the cash leg, and how the firm achieves legal and operational finality, applying the PFMI where it operates or relies on settlement infrastructure.
objectives: Design delivery versus payment and atomic settlement for tokenised trades
Evaluate cash leg options and their credit, liquidity and settlement risk
Assess legal and operational finality under different consensus models
syllabus: Delivery versus payment, atomic settlement and prefunding
Cash leg options: central bank money, tokenised deposits and stablecoins
Legal finality, probabilistic finality, forks and rollback
PFMI expectations for settlement, liquidity and operational risk

modules.title: Custody, Safekeeping and Client Asset Protection
modules.summary: How custodians, depositaries and platforms safeguard tokenised assets, from wallet architecture and key management to segregation, reconciliation and the return of client assets on insolvency.
objectives: Design a custody model and wallet architecture for tokenised assets
Implement key management, segregation and reconciliation controls
Evidence that client assets are protected and returnable on insolvency
syllabus: Custody models: direct holding, omnibus and third-party custodians
Private key management, multi-signature and threshold signatures
Reconciliation between the ledger and books and records
Client asset protection, insolvency and return of assets

modules.title: Smart Contracts, Interoperability and Technology Risk
modules.summary: The technology risks specific to tokenised products, including smart contract defects, administrative keys, oracles, bridges and fragmented ledgers, and the controls and assurance a firm should put in place.
objectives: Assess smart contract design, code audit and upgrade governance
Manage interoperability, bridge, oracle and node operator dependencies
Apply operational resilience and third-party risk controls to DLT arrangements
syllabus: Smart contract vulnerabilities, audits, pause functions and administrative keys
Fragmentation, cross-chain bridges and messaging standards
Oracles, data feeds and third-party technology providers
Incident response, cyber risk and resilience testing on a ledger

modules.title: Operating Model, Regulatory Engagement and Launch
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into an operating model and launch plan, covering governance, controls, financial crime, pilots and sandboxes, and how to engage the authority so that the product is approved and supervised with confidence.
objectives: Design the governance, controls and operating model for a tokenised product
Plan regulatory engagement, including pilots, sandboxes and permissions
Anticipate the questions a supervisor will ask and prepare the evidence
syllabus: Target operating model, risk appetite and board approval
Pilot regimes, sandboxes, permissions and exit routes
International work: FSB, IOSCO, CPMI and BIS on tokenisation
Workshop: a tokenised fund or bond launch reviewed through a supervisor's eyes
